Finnish Metals & Mining Sector Sees Steady Trade in First Half of 2024

HELSINKI, June 19 – Finland’s metals and mining industry posted stable trade figures for the first half of 2024, according to preliminary data released on Wednesday by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment. The sector, a key pillar of the Finnish economy, maintained its export and import volumes close to last year’s levels, despite fluctuating global market prices and modest domestic demand growth.

Total exports of metals and mining products reached EUR 3.15 billion in the first six months of the year, compared with EUR 3.12 billion during the same period in 2023, the ministry said. Imports totaled EUR 2.87 billion, a slight increase from EUR 2.81 billion last year, reflecting sustained demand for raw materials and equipment.

“The Finnish metals and mining industry continues to demonstrate resilience against external pressures,” said Tuomas Saarinen, Director of Industrial Policy at the ministry. “While price volatility in global markets has presented challenges, our export volumes have remained broadly stable, thanks in part to strong relationships with European partners.”

Nickel, copper, and zinc continued to dominate export shipments, with the bulk of deliveries destined for Germany, Sweden, and the Netherlands. Meanwhile, imports were primarily composed of iron ore, coal, and mining machinery sourced from Sweden, Russia, and Poland.

The Finnish Mining Association (FMA) also reported steady production levels among its member companies. “The first half of 2024 has been characterized by operational continuity across the sector,” said FMA Chairperson Helena Laaksonen. “Our mines and smelters have continued regular output, with no major interruptions or supply chain issues reported.”

Industry analysts pointed out that the subdued pace of global economic growth has kept commodity prices relatively stable in recent months, contributing to predictable trading patterns. “There has been little in the way of price shocks or sudden changes in demand for Finnish metals,” said Jari Mattila, a market analyst at Northstar Commodity Research. “This has allowed companies to plan production and logistics with a high degree of certainty.”

Employment in the sector remained steady at around 13,500 workers, in line with figures from late 2023, according to the Central Federation of Finnish Trade Unions. No major hiring or layoff announcements were reported during the period.

Looking ahead, industry representatives expressed cautious optimism. “We anticipate that current trading conditions will persist in the near future,” Laaksonen said. “As always, we are closely monitoring developments in major export markets, but for now, the outlook for Finnish metals and mining remains stable.”

Finland’s metals and mining industry accounts for approximately 6% of national exports and is considered a strategic sector for the country’s economy.
